claims: The derivatives of the actual fixed middle cutoff have C(N)*U^N bounds when the selected inverse width is at most U.
The angular jets of the exact mass integral divided by the actual middle mass are at most 2B: integration length cancels against the genuine I>=width/2 lower bound.
The exact balanced slope has every mixed derivative through N at most C(N)*U^N*B. High data B stay linear.

The existing normalized radial coordinate minus fst has every full derivative through N bounded by C(N)*(1+width)*U^N*B, where B bounds the actual endpoint-slope deviation jets. The width, total mass, interval, and map are unchanged.
limitations: The endpoint-slope deviation bound is a genuine intermediate source quantity, not a final transport or numerator bound. Its explicit Taylor trace instantiation and same-witness material estimate are subsequent steps.
All constants precede U, B, width, interval, and source data. No new collar or reference-state choice is made.
